_comment: Irregularities found by this session, published as found. A flag is not a defect in the site; it is a
fact about the world that a decision would otherwise step over. None of these blocks the merge, and
none of them is closed by editing a page - the 'next_step' column says what would actually close it.
status: open (needs a decision or new data), corrected (the register was amended), noted (no action
H01-H19 and Q19 are numbered to match the irregularity blocks inside injury_lab/raw/*.md, which cite
those ids. H20 is the correction log at the end of the Dallas capture. Do not renumber either side
without updating the other; check_site.py rule P5 fails the build when a cited id resolves nowhere.

flags.what: The official weekly injury report mutates under a fixed URL, and the mutation is now measured rather than asserted. Two independent records of the same URL one day apart differ on 18 of the 49 rows both of them hold: 15 rows carry a designation and an injury on 2026-11-13 that the 2026-11-12 record shows as blank, and 3 more differ on practice status. Two fixture-level record fields also differ.
flags.why_it_matters: A published row citing that URL cannot be re-checked after the page moves, so every number derived from it silently becomes unfalsifiable. Worse, two captures of one week are two different datasets, and a model trained on one and applied to the other is not the same model. The full comparison is on the audit page.
flags.evidence: injury_lab/data/transcribe_diff.json, produced by python3 -m injury_lab.transcribe from injury_lab/raw/2026-reg10-injuries.md and decision_lab/data/injuries.json
flags.next_step: Fix a snapshot day per fixture in the rules (see IG2 on the signals page and suggestion S19), and retain a dated capture for every transcription (S18).

flags.what: The page <title> does not match the week the page shows. /injuries/league/2025/reg01 is titled 'Week 10 of the 2025 Season' while its own heading reads 'Injuries - WEEK 1' and its fixtures are the 2025 opening week.
flags.why_it_matters: Any refresh job that reads the title to decide which week it fetched will label a season's first week as its tenth, and the error is invisible in the output because the URL is right.
flags.evidence: I03 extent field, and the two strings in the retained capture header
flags.next_step: Key automation on the URL and the fixture dates, never on the title. Published here so the next implementer does not rediscover it.

flags.what: The designation vocabulary is era-dependent. The 2015 page prints Out, Doubtful, Questionable and Probable; the 2026 capture in this repository printed only Out and Questionable across the fixtures retained, and no page in this capture set defines any of the four.
flags.why_it_matters: 'not Out' means something different in the two eras, and a rule written on Probable is undefined today. Any signal whose window crosses 2016 needs an era map, and the repository's own discovery / confirmation split sits exactly there.
flags.evidence: I04 versus I01; decision_lab flag D15 (official definitions never retrieved) is still open
flags.next_step: Retrieve the official definitions of each designation for each era, then either restrict the family to seasons with one vocabulary or publish the era map as data. Not done here rather than guessed here.

flags.what: All three retained weekly captures end at a chunk boundary, mid-table. The 2015 capture ends inside a URL, so the next fixture's two clubs are not even known; the 2026 capture ends inside the Chiefs table with Atlanta's table absent.
flags.why_it_matters: A truncated capture looks like a club with nothing to report. That is how 'we did not read it' becomes 'they are healthy', which is the failure mode the whole brief is trying to avoid.
flags.evidence: captures.json capture_gaps (3 records) and each capture file's trailing marker
flags.next_step: Fetch every chunk of a week before publishing it, and assert the row count against the page's own table count. capture.py fetch keeps the whole page for exactly this reason. The audit page shows the truncation did not cost rows here - all 49 rows this capture holds were also present in the other record - which is luck, not a reason to stop checking.

flags.what: The standing conclusion that the brief's 2nd/3rd/4th-string requirement is 'not satisfiable from official sources' is too strong. Three member clubs (Detroit, New England, Dallas) publish an ordered depth chart on the club's own domain, verified on 2026-11-13.
flags.why_it_matters: That conclusion is what had stopped every prior build from trying. It is recorded in decision_lab as flag D14 and question Q04, and in the board as a blocker, and it is wrong for at least the current season.
flags.next_step: Amend D14/Q04 in a future decision round to 'available for the current season from club publishers, with club-by-club provenance differences; not available for historical seasons from any source verified here'. This session records the correction rather than rewriting another session's register in place.

flags.what: Club depth charts are not one kind of object. Detroit's is 'Compiled by Lions Football Communications'; New England's states that it is 'published by the writers of Patriots.com', reflects 'the opinions of the Patriots.com writers' and does 'not necessarily reflect those of the organization'; Dallas's prints no statement at all.
flags.why_it_matters: A feature that treats 'depth chart on a club domain' as one source mixes a football-operations product with a disclaimer-bearing opinion page. Two clubs at the same position in the same week would not mean the same thing.
flags.evidence: verbatim provenance lines in each retained capture
flags.next_step: Classify every club chart by its own provenance sentence before any model reads it, and refuse the unattributed ones rather than averaging them in. Suggestion S16.

flags.what: Official page contradicts official page on the same player in the same week: the Week 10 report prints Kerby Joseph with 'Knee / Did Not Participate In Practice / Out', and the Lions' own depth chart has no Kerby Joseph row at all.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the same class of disagreement the decision pack recorded as D01-D03 between the injury report and NFL.com news pages. A model that trusts whichever page it read first will produce confident, contradictory inputs.
flags.evidence: I01 versus I05, both read 2026-11-13
flags.next_step: Publish both, name neither as truth, and let the absence be a feature only when both sources agree. The row is shown as 'designation with no slot on the chart' rather than dropped.

flags.what: There is no league-wide depth-chart schema. The three captured pages print 6, 5 and 4 string columns; Detroit lists WR three times with different occupancies; one club row has a single name and no second.
flags.why_it_matters: Any 'depth by string' number needs a per-club reader, so a 32-club capture is 32 parsers, not one. That is the real cost of the depth requirement, and it had never been measured.
flags.evidence: row_count and column counts in depth.json
flags.next_step: Write one reader per platform family and measure how many families cover 32 clubs before committing to a league-wide depth feature.

flags.what: Special-teams rows overlap the starting rows: Detroit lists Jack Fox as both P and H, and Jacob Saylors as KR first while DeAndre Carter is PR first and WR second.
flags.why_it_matters: Counting rows instead of players inflates any 'N players unavailable' feature, and a slot that is double-staffed in the chart is not two men deep.
flags.evidence: I05 special-teams block
flags.next_step: De-duplicate by player before counting, and publish the rule; no de-duplication rule is printed by any club.

flags.what: A club's own depth-chart URL failed while a sibling succeeded: www.newenglandpatriots.com/team/depth-chart returned HTTP 500 and www.patriots.com/team/depth-chart resolved, same club, same minute.
flags.why_it_matters: An availability sweep that records 5xx as 'this club publishes no depth chart' would understate coverage of the league and turn a server error into a finding about football.
flags.evidence: I07 versus I06
flags.next_step: Try every domain alias, and record transport failures as their own outcome, never as absence.

flags.what: The Patriots' QB row spans the chunk boundary of the fetched page: 'Drake Maye | Tommy DeVito' arrived in one chunk and the continuation naming Behren Morton in the next. From chunk 0 alone a reader cannot confirm that no fourth name follows Morton.
flags.why_it_matters: A chunk-level reader silently truncates a row, and a truncated depth row is exactly the kind of near-miss that reads as 'that club has two quarterbacks'.
flags.evidence: I06 extent chunks 0 and 1
flags.next_step: Reassemble by row, not by chunk, in the capture tool.

flags.what: The Patriots' chart defines LDE, RDE, ILB, RCB and LCB in its own legend, and then prints OLB, DT, LB, CB and S in its own table. The legend does not describe the table.
flags.why_it_matters: A join between a club's own legend and its own chart finds nothing, so a cross-club defensive-line count has no key. This is where depth features actually break.
flags.evidence: I06 legend block and defense block
flags.next_step: Either accept per-club label sets with no cross-club aggregation, or find a published crosswalk. None is cited anywhere in this capture set.

flags.what: Position disagreement between two official publishers for the same player in the same week: Ben Brown is printed as a C on the report and occupies LG first string and C second string on the club chart.
flags.why_it_matters: 'Who replaces the absent starter' depends on which slot you think he played. Two answers are both sourced.
flags.evidence: I01 Patriots row; I06 offense rows
flags.next_step: Publish every slot the player occupies, as this page does, instead of picking one.

flags.what: One player can fill two slots: Walter Rouse is listed as the second string at both LG and RG, and Gabe Jacas as the second string on two separate OLB rows.
flags.why_it_matters: Any 'backups available' count double-counts him by rows and under-counts what one absence costs by players. Both errors push a depth feature in opposite directions.
flags.evidence: I06 offense and defense blocks
flags.next_step: Define the counting rule as data before computing anything; no publisher states one.

flags.what: Returners double as starters: Marcus Jones is CB first string and PR first string on the same page, and Efton Chism III is a WR first string on one row and a WR second string on another.
flags.why_it_matters: A 'snap-weighted availability' feature built from these pages without de-duplication is wrong by construction, in a direction nobody can see.
flags.evidence: I06 offense and special-teams blocks
flags.next_step: De-duplicate by player id, which is the reason H21 matters.

flags.what: A refused join is published rather than smoothed: the 2026 Cowboys chart shares no player name or URL slug with this repository's 2025 Cowboys report rows, so no Dallas replacement row exists anywhere in this lab.
flags.why_it_matters: The tempting fix - join them anyway, they are both Cowboys - would produce a row that is true of neither season. Refusal needs to be visible or the next session will undo it.
flags.evidence: joined.json refused_joins
flags.next_step: Capture the 2026 Cowboys report week to make the join legitimate, or leave it refused.

flags.what: Three of the Cowboys' rows put two players in the same string cell (TE, LB, S). The page does not order inside a cell.
flags.why_it_matters: Taking the first link in such a cell invents a starter the club did not name. Plural 'co-starters' would be an interpretation too.
flags.evidence: I08 offense and defense blocks
flags.next_step: Publish the cell as ambiguous, which is what this lab does, and keep it out of any first-string count.

flags.what: Defensive-back labels mix CB, DB and S inside one unit on the same page, with no rule printed for what separates them.
flags.why_it_matters: 'Cornerback depth' is not countable across clubs, and F04 depends on it.
flags.evidence: I08 defense block
flags.next_step: Treat the labels as club-local and refuse cross-club aggregation until a published definition exists.

flags.what: Caleb Downs is the only entry in his row, labelled DB, with no second string and no definition anywhere on the page.
flags.why_it_matters: Whether that is a starter at safety or a nickel is unknown, and either reading changes the depletion count for the slot behind him.
flags.evidence: I08 defense block
flags.next_step: Left unmapped. A mapping would be a guess with a source link on it, which is worse than a blank.

flags.what: Correction log of the Dallas capture, kept because a self-audit is only worth publishing when it stays published. An earlier draft of that file recorded a malformed roster host in the CeeDee Lamb row as an irregularity of the source. Re-checked against the fetched text: the host in every row of that page is www.dallascowboys.com; the malformed string was introduced by this lab's own transcription, not published by the club. The claim is withdrawn, not deleted.
flags.why_it_matters: It is the error class no round-trip test can catch. Verifying a published row against the retained capture proves the row matches the capture; it cannot prove the capture matches the page. The one thing that can is a second, independent record - which is why the cross-capture audit on this site exists.
flags.evidence: correction log block at the end of injury_lab/raw/2026-depth-dal.md
flags.next_step: Keep the correction in place, and prefer cross-capture comparison to self-comparison wherever a second record exists.

flags.what: Neither publisher gives a player identifier. The report links nfl.com/players/kevin-byard/ while the chart links patriots.com/team/players-roster/kevin-byard-iii/, and the report prints 'Kevin Byard'; elsewhere the reverse happens - 'Ben Brown' with slug ben-brown-2 on the report against slug ben-brown on the chart. A join on name or on slug each drops a row this lab can only recover by trying both.
flags.why_it_matters: At capture scale, name-based joins quietly lose designations, and a lost designation looks like an available player. This is the mechanism by which an injury model decays without any error appearing anywhere.
flags.evidence: replacements.json match_key_used field: 1 of the 17 rows was found by slug only, 1 by name only, 5 rows have no chart row at all
flags.next_step: Obtain a stable player ID from an official publisher and key every join on it. Question Q20.

flags.what: The strategy-ID collision the board narrates as flag X01 is quantified: 15 rule numbers are used by more than one ledger with different rule names attached. S1 is 'Elo margin vs closing spread' in two ledgers and 'Own line vs close: 3+ pt edge' in a third.
flags.why_it_matters: Scoring one rule from the wrong ledger is not a rounding error; the board's own arithmetic for X01 is -0.0873 instead of +0.0430.
flags.evidence: builds.json strategy_id_collisions, recomputed from data/derived/bets.csv, line_lab/data/derived/bets.csv, data/derived/gates_results.csv and reports/strategies.json
flags.next_step: Namespace every strategy ID by build (LL-S1, PIPE-S01, VFY-V01, INJ-F01) at the generator level, so a collision is impossible rather than merely documented. Suggestion S15.

flags.what: New finding, not previously recorded anywhere in this repository: the two gate registers use the same IDs for different rules. G1 is 'Sample size' in scripts/gates.py and 'Provenance' in docs/preregistration.md; all eight collide.
flags.why_it_matters: 'This strategy passed G4' means 'ROI positive in the confirmation window' in one build and 'holdout ROI > 0' in another. A promotion rule written on a gate ID can be satisfied by the wrong gate, and the site would report a pass that never happened.
flags.evidence: builds.json gate_id_collisions, computed from both files
flags.next_step: Rename to distinct gate namespaces and rewrite every 'passed Gn' claim as a citable threshold. This lab already uses IG1..IG9 and cites the source of each threshold.

flags.what: Dated, numbered weekly club documents exist on the NFL club-media CDN - Green Bay's 'Dope Sheet' for 2025 Preseason Game 1 arrived as one asset at a stable URL, and its own contents list a DEPTH CHART section. The depth block itself was not in the chunk read here.
flags.why_it_matters: If every club publishes a dated weekly chart somewhere in this form, a historical depth-conditional backtest becomes possible and the depth part of this brief stops being forward-only. If not, it stays a live-snapshot feature. Nobody in this repository has established which.
flags.evidence: I09, chunk 0 of 22
flags.next_step: Open one dope sheet per club for a dated week and record whether it carries an ordered chart. Question Q21; this lab publishes the URL and the fact that it resolved, and nothing about depth ordering from it.

flags.what: Every rule in the injury family fails the sample gate and nothing is promoted: six completed fixtures in the pinned dataset match a retained official capture, against a 300-bet requirement. The pilot's most flattering number, +0.63 units per bet over 6 bets from a rule deliberately designed to be meaningless, is published here as the reason to distrust small n.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the arithmetic of luck. A no-information control wins five of six bets at the recorded closing prices; any page that showed that as a strategy would be indistinguishable from noise dressed as a model.
flags.evidence: signals.json family rows, F05 in particular
flags.next_step: Run the capture at scale (weeks needed are on the capture page), then the gates. No shortcut, and no reward.

flags.what: The three 2026 fixtures this lab can join carry no line, no price and no score in the pinned dataset, because the games had not been played at retrieval time. Every market cell on those rows is blank.
flags.why_it_matters: Origination for the current week cannot be scored against anything inside this repository. It can be originated and published; it cannot be validated until the results and prices exist.
flags.evidence: joined.json game_features played=false rows
flags.next_step: Nothing is imputed. Re-run the join after the pinned dataset updates.

flags.what: The weekly report is a practice and designation report for an upcoming fixture, not a record of who actually did not play. 'Out' is an intent published before the game; the game's own inactive list is a different document and is not in this capture set.
flags.why_it_matters: A backtest that treats a designation as an outcome measures the report, not the football. An injury signal can look sharp because designations were accurate and still lose money on the games where they were not.
flags.evidence: I01/I03/I04 page structure: Practice Status and Game Status columns, no result column
flags.next_step: Find the official source for game inactives and capture it alongside the report. Question Q22.

flags.what: This directory publishes no reward amounts, no payouts and no prize tiers. The competition page in the consolidated dashboard carries an unfunded structure and this lab does not restate it in numbers.
flags.why_it_matters: A leaderboard with a number next to 'reward' invites a decision nobody has authorised.
flags.evidence: by design; check_site.py rule P13 fails the build on any currency amount
flags.next_step: Owner decision, after the gates have been passed by something.

flags.what: Retention asymmetry between two transcriptions of the same official page. decision_lab/data/injuries.json holds 254 rows of the Week 10 2026 report and is cited as the repository's injury evidence, but no raw page text was retained with it; injury_lab/raw/2026-reg10-injuries.md holds 49 rows of the same page with a SHA-256 and a byte count.
flags.why_it_matters: The larger file can be compared but never re-verified, and the smaller one can be checked line by line. Once the page moves - and H01 shows it moves within a day - a transcription without its capture is an assertion. Any decision that rests on such a table rests on a recollection.
flags.evidence: ls decision_lab/raw 2>/dev/null prints nothing; injury_lab/data/raw_index.json lists 6 hashed captures
flags.next_step: Make retention a build requirement for every injury row published anywhere in this repository: a row without a capture that contains it is published as unverified. Suggestion S18; the round-trip rule already runs here as check_site.py P7.

flags.what: 23 of the 139 captured report rows carry a position code that no captured page defines (DE, T, G among them), so their unit is blank and they are excluded from every unit-scoped count.
flags.why_it_matters: The brief asks specifically about deficiencies in the defensive front, and DE is the code that says defensive end. A unit feature that quietly excludes the unlabeled codes measures a different population than the one it claims to.
flags.evidence: captures.json unit coverage; conventions.py refuses unmapped codes by design
flags.next_step: Retrieve an official position-code definition page and map by citation, or restrict unit claims to the codes that are defined. Both options are open; neither is taken here. Question Q24.
